# Thok Nath (Nuer Language) Grammar Rules
**Compiled from: Nuer Bible (RUAC KUƆTH IN RƐL RƆ), African Storybook Project, and Ethio Language Box**

---

## SECTION 1: THE WRITING SYSTEM AND SPECIAL CHARACTERS

Thok Nath uses the Latin alphabet with several special characters and diacritics:

| Character | Notes |
|-----------|-------|
| ɛ / Ɛ | open-mid front vowel (like "e" in "bed") |
| ɔ / Ɔ | open-mid back vowel (like "o" in "law") |
| ä / ë / ö | vowels with umlaut marks |
| ɣ / Ɣ | voiced velar fricative |
| ŋ / Ŋ | velar nasal (like "ng" in "sing") |
| ɛ̈ | ɛ with umlaut |
| i̱ / u̱ / a̱ | letters with a sub-bar (retroflex quality) |
| Long vowels | written by doubling: aa, ee, oo, ɛɛ, ɔɔ, ii, uu |
| / (slash) | marks negative particles in some notations |

---

## SECTION 2: PRONOUNS

### 2.1 Subject Pronouns

| Nuer | English |
|------|---------|
| Ɣän | I |
| Kɔn / Nɛy | We |
| Ji̱n | You (singular, male or female) |
| Jɛn | He / She |
| Yiɛn | You (plural) |
| Kɛn | They |

> **Note:** Nuer does not distinguish male/female in third-person singular — **Jɛn** = He and She.

### 2.2 Object Pronouns (short forms used after negators and verbs)

| Subject Form | Object / Short Form |
|---|---|
| Ɣän (I) | ɣä |
| Kɔn / Nɛy (We) | kɔ / nɛy |
| Ji̱n (You sg.) | ji̱ |
| Jɛn (He/She) | jɛ |
| Yiɛn (You pl.) | yiɛ |
| Kɛn (They) | kɛ |

> Examples from Bible/stories:
> - *Cä ɣä lar* – "I told myself"
> - *Cuɛ jɛ nöŋ wut* – "He brought him to the man"
> - *Cuɛ kɛ poth* – "He blessed them"

### 2.3 Possessive Pronouns

Possessives are formed with **Duŋ-** prefix plus a person-marker suffix, or directly as noun suffixes:

| Nuer | English | Example |
|------|---------|---------|
| Duŋdä | My | Bokdä = My book |
| Duŋda | Our | Bokda = Our book |
| Duŋdu | Your (sg.) | Bokdu = Your book |
| Garɛ | His | (irregular) |
| Nyamɛ | Her | (irregular) |
| Duŋdun | Your (pl.) | Bokdun = Your (pl.) book |
| Duŋdiɛn | Their | Bokdiɛn = Their book |

**Possessive is also expressed as a SUFFIX on the noun:**

| Suffix | Meaning | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| -dä / -kä | my | ciaaŋdä = my home, ciëŋmaari = my family, dhɔrä = my home |
| -du | your (sg.) | ciaaŋdu = your home |
| -dɛ | his/her | ciaaŋdɛ = his/her home |
| -da / -dan | our | ciaaŋdan = our home |
| -dun | your (pl.) | |
| -diɛn | their | dhɔaardiɛn = their family |

> Examples from texts:
> - *gua̱ndi̱t* = the elder/old man (literally "big father" — possessive suffix on noun)
> - *gatdɛ* = his child/son
> - *ciekdɛ* = his wife
> - *bokdä* = my book
> - *manikiɛn* = their mother

### 2.3.1 Inherently Possessive Kinship Terms — Do NOT Add `-dä`

Certain kinship terms in Thok Nath **already encode "my"** as part of the word root. They should **never** take the `-dä` possessive suffix — doing so is redundant and incorrect.

**Verified from Nyawal's family (ASB — *Ɛ ɣän Nyawal.* storybook):**

| Thok Nath | English | WRONG form |
|-----------|---------|------------|
| `maar` | my mother | ~~maardä~~ |
| `gua̱a̱r` | my father | ~~gua̱a̱rdä~~ |
| `dämaar` | my brother | ~~dämaardä~~ (suppletive: your = dämuɔɔr, his/her = däman) |
| `nyi̱maar` | my sister | ~~nyi̱maardä~~ (suppletive: his/her = nyi̱man) |
| `maadɔɔŋ` | my grandmother | ~~maadɔɔŋdä~~ |
| `gua̱a̱dɔɔŋ` | my grandfather | ~~gua̱a̱dɔɔŋdä~~ |
| `gua̱a̱len` | my uncle | ~~gua̱a̱lendä~~ |
| `maalen` | my aunt | ~~maalendä~~ |
| `ciëŋmaari` | my family | ~~ciëŋmaaridä~~ |

> **Source sentences (ASB):**
> - *Mɛmɛ ɛ maar.* = "This is my mother." ✓ (NOT *Mɛmɛ ɛ maardä*)
> - *Mɛmɛ ɛ gua̱a̱r.* = "This is my father." ✓
> - *Mɛmɛ ɛ dämaar.* = "This is my brother." ✓
> - *Mɛmɛ ɛ nyimaar.* = "This is my sister." ✓
> - *Dämaar ni Lual ɛ camjiɛc.* = "My brother Lual was very greedy." ✓
> - *Ti̱ti̱ kɛ ciëŋmaari.* = "This is my family." ✓

> **Critical note on `dämaar`:** The `dä-` at the start is part of the kinship root (it means "brother"), **NOT** the possessive suffix `-dä`. It cannot be detached or doubled. `dämaar` ≠ `dä` + `maar`. The forms are suppletive: dämaar (my), dämuɔɔr (your), däman (his/her).

**These kinship terms are suppletive — the whole word changes by possessor. Do NOT add `-dɛ` suffix.**

**Mother — suppletive forms (confirmed: Bible GEN.2.24, GEN.3.20; ASB throughout):**

| Thok Nath | English |
|-----------|---------|
| `maar` | my mother |
| `man` | his/her mother |
| `manikiɛn` | their mother |

> Bible: *bi wut gua̱n kɛnɛ man ba̱ny piny* = "a man leaves his father and **mother**" (GEN.2.24)
> ASB: *man Bol* = "Bol's mother" | *man kɛnɛ gua̱n* = "mother and father"

**Father — suppletive forms (confirmed: Bible GEN.2.24; ASB throughout):**

| Thok Nath | English |
|-----------|---------|
| `gua̱a̱r` | my father |
| `gua̱n` | his/her father |

> Bible: *bi wut gua̱n kɛnɛ man ba̱ny piny* = "a man leaves his **father** and mother" (GEN.2.24)
> ASB: *gua̱n kakä* = "the farmer" (lit. "father of the field") | *man kɛnɛ gua̱n* = "mother and father"

**Brother — suppletive forms:**

| Thok Nath | English |
|-----------|---------|
| `dämaar` | my brother |
| `dämuɔɔr` | your brother |
| `däman` | his/her brother |

---

### 2.4 Reflexive Pronouns

Formed with **puɔ̱ny** + possessive suffix:

| Nuer | English |
|------|---------|
| Ɣän puɔ̱ny dä | I myself |
| Kɔn puɔ̱nydan | We ourselves |
| Ji̱n puɔ̱nydu | You yourself |
| Jɛn puɔ̱nydɛ | He/She himself/herself |
| Yiɛn puɔ̱nydun | You yourselves |
| Kɛn pua̱ny kiɛn | They themselves |

## SECTION 3: SENTENCE STRUCTURE (WORD ORDER)

### 3.1 The Fundamental Distinction: SOV vs. SVO

Thok Nath is primarily a **Verb-Second / Subject-Object-Verb** language in certain constructions, but exhibits **Subject-Verb-Object** in others. The key patterns:

**PRESENT TENSE AFFIRMATIVE:** `La + Subject + Object + Verb`
- *La ɣän wargak lääri̱ ɛ kuɛɛn ni̱ ciaŋ.* = "I read newspaper every day."
- *La jɛn wargak lääri̱ ɛ kuɛɛn ni̱ ciaŋ.* = "He reads newspaper every day."
- *La ɣän ɛ mi̱th.* = "I eat."

**PAST TENSE AFFIRMATIVE:** `Subject + PAST-MARKER + Object + Verb`
- *Ɣän cä wargak lääri̱ kuɛn pan.* = "I read newspaper yesterday."
- *Jɛn cɛ wargak lääri̱ kuɛn pan.* = "He read newspaper yesterday."

**PRESENT CONTINUOUS:** `Subject + ɛ + Object + Verb`
- *Ɣän ɛ kuɛɛn wargak lääri̱ ni̱.* = "I am reading newspaper."
- *Jɛn ɛ kuɛɛn wargak lääri̱ ni̱.* = "He is reading newspaper."

**FUTURE TENSE AFFIRMATIVE:** `Subject + FUTURE-MARKER + Object + Verb`
- *Ɣän bä wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun.* = "I will read newspaper tomorrow."
- *Jɛn bɛ wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun.* = "He will read newspaper tomorrow."

**Narrative Past (Bible/Stories):** `Cu/Cuɛ + Subject + Object + Verb`
- *Cu Kuoth buay nɛn gɔaaɛ.* = "God saw that the light was good."
- *Cu mandɔɔŋ gaak kä cuɛ rɔal.* = "Grandmother became angry and shouted."
- *Cu wut jɛ naŋ pa̱a̱m.* = "The man took him to the rock."

> **KEY INSIGHT:** The narrative past marker **cu/cuɛ** is a past completive marker that comes BEFORE the subject in formal/narrative speech (especially the Bible). In everyday past speech, the marker comes AFTER the subject: *Ɣän cä...*, *Jɛn cɛ...*

### 3.2 Sentence Pattern Summary Table

| Tense / Form | Nuer Pattern | Key Marker |
|---|---|---|
| Present Affirmative | La + S + O + V | **La** (topic marker) |
| Present Negative | /Ci̱ + S + O + V | **Ci̱/Cɛ/Cän** |
| Present Continuous Affirm. | S + ɛ + O + V | **ɛ** |
| Present Continuous Neg. | S + /cɛ/cän + O + V | **cɛ / cän / ci̱** |
| Past Affirmative | S + PAST-MKR + O + V | see §4.2 |
| Past Negative | S + /kän/käni̱/ka̱n + O + V | see §4.3 |
| Past Continuous Affirm. | S + V-marked + O + ɛnëë | **ɛnëë** |
| Past Continuous Neg. | S + /kän + O + ɛnëë | **kän/käni̱/ka̱n** |
| Future Affirm. | S + FUTURE-MKR + O + V | see §4.4 |
| Future Negative | S + /cɛ/cän/ci̱ + O + bi̱ + V | **bi̱ + negation** |
| Narrative Past (formal) | Cu/Cuɛ + S + O + V | **Cu / Cuɛ** |

---

## SECTION 4: TENSE MARKERS (AUXILIARY / PRE-VERB MARKERS)

### 4.1 The "To Be" Copula (Present)

**Positive:** Uses **Ɛ** (singular) or **Kɛ** (plural)

| Subject | To Be | Example |
|---------|-------|---------|
| Ɣän (I) | Ɛ | Ɛ ɣän. = "I am." |
| Ji̱n (You) | Ɛ | Ɛ ji̱n. = "You are." |
| Jɛn (He/She) | Ɛ (after subject) | Jɛn ɛ. = "He/She is." |
| Kɔn (We) | Kɛ | Kɛ kɔn. = "We are." |
| Yiɛn (You pl.) | Kɛ | Kɛ yiɛn. = "You (pl.) are." |
| Kɛn (They) | Kɛ | Kɛn kɛ. / Kɛ kɛn. = "They are." |

> **Rule:** For I/You/He/She: **Ɛ** precedes I/You or follows He/She. For We/You(pl)/They: **Kɛ** is used.

**With complement (noun/adjective):**
- *Ɛ ɣän ŋi̱i̱c.* = "I am a teacher."
- *Jɛn ɛ ŋi̱i̱c.* = "He/She is a teacher."
- *Kɛ kɔn ŋi̱ääc.* = "We are teachers."
- *Ɛ ɣän Nyawal.* = "I am Maria." (from storybook)
- *Mɛmɛ ɛ maar.* = "This is my mother."

**Negative Present "To Be":** Uses **/Ciɛɛ** (singular) or **/Ci̱kɛ** (plural)

| Nuer | English |
|------|---------|
| /Ciɛɛ ɣän. | I am not. |
| /Ci̱kɛ kɔn. | We are not. |
| /Ciɛɛ ji̱n. | You are not. |
| /Ciɛɛ jɛn. | He/She is not. |
| /Ci̱kɛ yiɛn. | You (pl.) are not. |
| /Ci̱kɛ kɛn. | They are not. |

> Alternative negative form seen: **/Ciɛ** (uniform for all subjects in some registers):
> - */Ciɛ ɣän.* = "I am not."
> - */Ciɛ kɔn.* = "We are not."

### 4.2 Past Tense Markers (Positive)

**"To Be" Past Positive:** **Ci̱** (uniform for all subjects)

| Nuer | English |
|------|---------|
| Ci̱ ɣän. | I was. |
| Ci̱ nɛy. | We were. |
| Ci̱ ji̱n. | You were. |
| Ci̱ jɛn. | He/She was. |
| Ci̱ yiɛn. | You (pl.) were. |
| Ci̱ kɛn. | They were. |

**Action Past Tense Markers** — the marker changes by person:

| Subject | Past Marker | Example |
|---------|-------------|---------|
| Ɣän (I) | cä | Ɣän **cä** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn pan. |
| Kɔn/Nɛy (We) | ci̱ nɛy | Kɔn **ci̱ nɛy** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn pan. |
| Ji̱n (You sg.) | ci̱ | Ji̱n **ci̱** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn pan. |
| Jɛn (He/She) | cɛ | Jɛn **cɛ** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn pan. |
| Yiɛn (You pl.) | cia | Yiɛn **cia** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn pan. |
| Kɛn (They) | ci̱ kɛn | Kɛn **ci̱ kɛn** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn pan. |

> **Rule Summary:**
> - I → **cä**
> - He/She → **cɛ**
> - You (sg.) + They → **ci̱**
> - We → **ci̱ nɛy**
> - You (pl.) → **cia**

**Narrative past (Cu/Cuɛ):** Used in formal narrative and Bible texts, placed BEFORE the subject:
- *Cu Kuoth wee i̱...* = "And God said..."
- *Cuɛ jɛ cam.* = "He ate it."
- *Cu nɛy ɛ lar mandɔɔŋ.* = "We told grandmother."
- *Cu wut jɛ naŋ pa̱a̱m.* = "The man took him to the rock."

### 4.3 Past Tense Negative Markers

| Subject | Negative Marker | Example |
|---------|----------------|---------|
| Ɣän (I) | /ka̱n | Ɣän **/ka̱n** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn pan. |
| Kɔn (We) | /kän nɛy | Kɔn **/kän nɛy** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn pan. |
| Ji̱n (You sg.) | /käni̱ | Ji̱n **/käni̱** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn pan. |
| Jɛn (He/She) | /känɛ | Jɛn **/känɛ** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn pan. |
| Yiɛn (You pl.) | /kän yiɛn | Yiɛn **/kän yiɛn** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn pan. |
| Kɛn (They) | /kän kɛn | Kɛn **/kän kɛn** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn pan. |

> Examples from sources:
> - */Ka̱n lɔ̱ŋ ɛn wa̱lɛ.* = "I did not rest today." (Donkey & Ox storybook)
> - *Gaat /ci kɛn jɛ gör.* = "The children did not want to leave."

**"To Be" Past Negative:** **/Kän** (uniform for all subjects)
- */Kän ɣän.* = "I was not."
- */Kän jɛn kɔnɛ däktör.* = "He was not a doctor."

### 4.4 Future Tense Markers (Positive)

| Subject | Future Marker | Example |
|---------|--------------|---------|
| Ɣän (I) | bä | Ɣän **bä** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun. |
| Kɔn (We) | bi̱ nɛy | Kɔn **bi̱ nɛy** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun. |
| Ji̱n (You sg.) | bi̱ | Ji̱n **bi̱** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun. |
| Jɛn (He/She) | bɛ | Jɛn **bɛ** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun. |
| Yiɛn (You pl.) | bia | Yiɛn **bia** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun. |
| Kɛn (They) | bi̱ kɛn | Kɛn **bi̱ kɛn** wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun. |

> **Rule Summary:**
> - I → **bä**
> - He/She → **bɛ**
> - You (sg.) → **bi̱**
> - We → **bi̱ nɛy**
> - You (pl.) → **bia**
> - They → **bi̱ kɛn**

> Examples from sources:
> - *Ɣän bä yik wä.* = "I must go." / "I will go."
> - *Jɛn bɛ wä.* = "He will go."
> - *Bɛ ben.* = "He/She will come." (from storybooks)
> - *Bä ji̱ luäk.* = "I will help you."
> - *Ɣän bä wä lät i̱ruun.* = "I will go to work tomorrow." / "I will be going to work tomorrow."

> **CRITICAL RULE — Future vs. Future Continuous:**
> Thok Nath does NOT require the continuous verb form **wa̱a̱** in the future, even when English says "will be going." The simple future marker **bä/bɛ/bi̱** already covers both "will" and "will be going." Always use the simple verb root:
> - CORRECT: *Ɣän bä wä lät i̱ruun.* = "I will be going to work tomorrow."
> - AVOID: *Ɣän bä wa̱a̱ lät i̱ruun.* (overly specifying continuous in future is unnatural)
>
> This is confirmed by the Bible (Gen 6:17): `ɣän bä wi̱c muɔ̱ɔ̱n moc nyɔc` = "I am going to bring floodwaters" — the English "going to" / future continuous is rendered simply as **bä + verb root**.

### 4.5 Present Negative Markers

| Subject | Negative Marker |
|---------|----------------|
| Ɣän (I) | /cän or /ci̱ |
| Kɔn (We) | /ci̱ nɛy |
| Ji̱n (You sg.) | /ci̱ |
| Jɛn (He/She) | /cɛ |
| Yiɛn (You pl.) | /ci̱ yiɛn |
| Kɛn (They) | /ci̱ kɛn |

> Examples:
> - *Ɣän /cän jɛ kuɛn.* = "I do not read."
> - *Jɛn /cɛ jɛ kuɛn.* = "She does not read."
> - */Ci̱ ji̱n wargak lääri̱ ɛ kuɛɛn ni ciaŋ.* = "You do not read newspaper every day."

### 4.6 Present Continuous Verb Endings

In present continuous, the verb ROOT takes a suffix based on person:

| Subject | Verb Ending | Example (root: lät "make") |
|---------|-------------|---------------------------|
| Ɣän (I) | -ä | lätd**ä** / gɔ̱a̱r**ä** |
| Ji̱n (You sg.) | -i̱ | lätd**i̱** / gɔ̱ɔ̱r**i̱** |
| Jɛn (He/She) | -ɛ | lätd**ɛ** / gɔ̱ɔ̱r**ɛ** |
| Kɔn / Yiɛn / Kɛn | unchanged | lät kɛnɛ / gɔ̱ɔ̱r kɛnɛ |

> Examples:
> - *Ɣän lätdä jɛ.* = "I am making it."
> - *Ji̱n lätdi̱ jɛ.* = "You are making it."
> - *Jɛn lätdɛ jɛ.* = "He/She is making it."
> - *Kɔn lät nɛyɛ.* = "We are making."

### 4.7 Past Continuous — "ɛnëë"

Past continuous is indicated by adding **ɛnëë** ("was/were") at the end of the sentence. The verb takes the same personal endings as present continuous:

- *Ɣän kuɛ̈ɛ̈nä wargak lääri̱ ɛnëë.* = "I was reading newspaper."
- *Jɛn kuɛɛnɛ wargak lääri̱ ɛnëë.* = "He was reading newspaper."
- *Kɔn kuɛɛn nɛy wargak lääri̱ ɛnëë.* = "We were reading newspaper."

---

## SECTION 5: POSSESSION — "TO HAVE"

### 5.1 Positive "Have"

The verb "to have" varies by person:

| Subject | Have Form | Example |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| Ɣän (I) | ta̱a̱ | Ɣän **ta̱a̱** kɛ galam. = "I have a pen." |
| Ji̱n (You sg.) | ti̱i̱ | Ji̱n **ti̱i̱** kɛ galam. = "You have a pen." |
| Jɛn (He/She) | tëë | Jɛn **tëë** kɛ galam. = "He/She has a pen." |
| Kɔn (We) | te kɔn / te nɛy | Kɔn **te kɔn** kɛ galam. = "We have a pen." |
| Yiɛn (You pl.) | te yiɛn | Yiɛn **te yiɛn** kɛ galam. |
| Kɛn (They) | te kɛn | Kɛn **te kɛn** kɛ galam. = "They have a pen." |

> **Rule:** Singular → **ta̱a̱ / ti̱i̱ / tëë** (varying by person). Plural → **te** + pronoun.

> From storybook: *Ta̱a̱kɛ mäthni da̱ŋ ŋuaan.* = "I have four friends."

### 5.2 Negative "Have" (Do Not Have)

Uses **/thiɛlɛ** + short object pronoun (uniform marker):

| Nuer | English |
|------|---------|
| Ɣän /thiɛlɛ ɣä galam. | I do not have a pen. |
| Kɔn /thiɛlɛ kɔn galam. | We do not have a pen. |
| Ji̱n /thiɛlɛ ji̱ galam. | You do not have a pen. |
| Jɛn /thiɛlɛ jɛ galam. | He/She does not have a pen. |
| Yiɛn /thiɛlɛ yiɛ galam. | You (pl.) do not have a pen. |
| Kɛn /thiɛlɛ kɛ galam. | They do not have a pen. |

### 5.3 Past Negative "Had Not" (Did Not Have)

Uses **/cɛ te kɛ** + short pronoun + **ɛnëë**:

| Nuer | English |
|------|---------|
| Ɣän /cɛ te kɛ ɣä ɛnëë. | I did not have. |
| Ji̱n /cɛ te kɛ ji̱ ɛnëë. | You did not have. |
| Jɛn /cɛ te kɛ jɛ ɛnëë. | He/She did not have. |
| Kɛn /cɛ te kɛkɛ ɛnëë. | They did not have. |

---

## SECTION 6: NEGATION — COMPLETE SYSTEM

### 6.1 Negation Summary Table

| Context | I | You (sg.) | He/She | We | You (pl.) | They |
|---------|---|-----------|--------|----|-----------|----|
| Present "be" | /Ciɛɛ | /Ciɛɛ | /Ciɛɛ | /Ci̱kɛ | /Ci̱kɛ | /Ci̱kɛ |
| Past "be" | /Kän | /Kän | /Kän | /Kän | /Kän | /Kän |
| Present action | /cän | /ci̱ | /cɛ | /ci̱ nɛy | /ci̱ yiɛn | /ci̱ kɛn |
| Past action | /ka̱n | /käni̱ | /känɛ | /kän nɛy | /kän yiɛn | /kän kɛn |
| Future action | /cän + bi̱ | /ci̱ + bi̱ | /cɛ + bi̱ | /ci̱ nɛy + bi̱ | /cia + bi̱ | /ci̱ kɛn + bi̱ |
| Have (present) | /thiɛlɛ | /thiɛlɛ | /thiɛlɛ | /thiɛlɛ | /thiɛlɛ | /thiɛlɛ |

> **Key Pattern:** The negation marker **always includes a person indicator** in action tenses, but is **uniform** for "to be" (Ciɛɛ/Ci̱kɛ, Kän) and "have not" (thiɛlɛ).

---

## SECTION 7: INTERROGATIVE (QUESTION) FORMS

### 7.1 Question Formation

Thok Nath **does not use auxiliary inversion** to form questions. The declarative word order is kept; questions are signaled by:
1. **Rising intonation** in speech
2. **Question mark (?)** in writing
3. **Question words** at the start or end of the clause

> Examples:
> - *La ɣän wargak lääri̱ ɛ kuɛɛn ni̱ ciaŋ?* = "Do I read newspaper every day?" (same as declarative + ?)
> - *Ɣän bä wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun?* = "Will I read newspaper tomorrow?"
> - *Jɛn bɛ wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun?* = "Will he read newspaper tomorrow?"

### 7.2 Question Words

| Nuer | English | Example |
|------|---------|---------|
| ŋu? / Ɛŋu? | What? | *Ɛŋu εn nεmɔ?* = "What is that?" |
| ŋa? / Ɛŋa? | Who? | *Ɛŋa ci dɔw jiaath kac ɔ?* = "Who bit the fruits?" |
| Nεy? | When? | *Bịben ị nεy?* = "When will you come?" |
| Gua̱th ε mith? | Where? | *Nyawdä ɛ nikä?* = "Where is my cat?" |
| I̱di̱? | How? | *Tëk tëë dị?* = "How is life?" |
| Ɛŋu / ɣöö di̱? | Why? | *Ɛŋu mi̱ la jäny kε jε?* = "Why is he late?" |
| Lotε ŋa? | Whom? | |
| Ɛduŋ ŋa? | Whose? | |
| Min diεn? | Which? | |

> More question examples from sources:
> - *Ji̱n a ni kä?* = "Where are you?" (God calls Adam, Gen 3:9)
> - *Cɔal kε ciöt du ịdị?* = "What is your name?"
> - *I̱di̱ ci kɔn jek?* = "How did we find it?"
> - *Ɛŋu ci lɛl ɛ!* = "What is this you have done!" (Gen 3:13)

## SECTION 8: NOUNS — SINGULAR, PLURAL, AND MODIFICATION

### 8.1 Plural Formation

Nuer plurals are complex and often irregular. Common patterns observed:

| Singular | Plural | Pattern |
|----------|--------|---------|
| ŋi̱i̱c (teacher) | ŋi̱ääc (teachers) | vowel change |
| gääth (merchant) | ga̱a̱th (merchants) | vowel shift |
| däktör (doctor) | däktöri̱ (doctors) | add -i̱ |
| wut (man) | wutni (men) | add -ni |
| ciek (woman) | mänkɛ (women) | suppletive |
| gat (child) | gaat / gaatkiɛn | vowel change / suffix |
| jiath (tree) | jiɛn (trees) | suppletive |
| buɔk / bok (book) | buɔkni (books) | add -ni |
| rɛc (fish) | rɛc yiëri (fish - collective) | |
| le̱y (animal/creature) | le̱e̱yni (animals) | add -ni |
| naath (person/Nuer person) | naath (people) | same form |
| wargak (paper/newspaper) | wargakni | add -ni |
| diit (bird) | diit (birds) | same |

> **Rule:** Many plurals add **-ni** or **-kiɛn** as a suffix. Others involve vowel alternation (especially long vowel → different vowel pattern). Some are suppletive (completely different words).

### 8.2 Noun Modifiers (Adjectives)

Adjectives typically **follow** the noun they modify in Nuer:

- *wut mi di̱i̱t* = "a big/old man" (wut = man, mi di̱i̱t = which is big)
- *duël mi tɔt* = "a small house" (tɔt = small)
- *duël mi di̱i̱t* = "a big house"
- *lony kɛl* = "one lion" (kɛl = one, follows noun)
- *thäk mi dɔaaŋ* = "an old ox"
- *ciek mi di̱i̱t* = "an old woman"
- *thuɔ̱rbiɛl mi tɔ̱c mi di̱i̱t* = "big blue bus" (two adjectives follow)

**Linking adjective with "mi" (which/that is):**
- *le̱y mi pɛl kɛ pɛl* = "creature which is crafty"
- *naath tin tëk rɛy pi̱i̱ni* = "living creatures in the water"
- *jiath mi moc naath ŋäc gɔyni kɛnɛ jiäk* = "the tree of knowledge of good and evil"

### 8.3 Noun Possession / Genitive

Possession is shown by **juxtaposition** (noun + possessive suffix) or by **noun + dɛ/da/du + noun**:

- *gua̱ndi̱t* = "the elder" (literally: "father-big")
- *ciëŋ mandɔɔŋdiɛn* = "their grandmother's home"
- *duëëlgɔ̱rä* = "my school" (duëël = house/building + gɔ̱r = learning + -ä = my)
- *bieyni duëëlgɔ̱rkädu* = "your school uniform"
- *thurbil in tɔ̱c in di̱i̱t* = "the big blue bus" (article + adj + adj following)

### 9.2 Verb "Say/Speak" in Biblical Narrative

The Bible uses a consistent formula for direct speech:
- **Cu X wee i̱, "..."** = "And X said, '...'"
- **Cu X jiök i̱, "..."** = "And X said to [someone], '...'"
- **Cu X loc i̱, "..."** = "And X replied, '...'"
- **Cu X cu jɛ thiec i̱, "..."** = "And X asked [someone], '...'"

> Examples:
> - *Cu Kuoth wee i̱, "A ɣɔw tekɛ buay."* = "God said, 'Let there be light.'"
> - *Cu wut jɛ cu wee i̱, "Kitdɛ..."* = "The man said, 'This is now...'"
> - *Cu Kuoth Nhial ni Kuoth jɛ luek ɛ bum ɛlɔ̱ŋ wee i̱...* = "The Lord God commanded the man..."

## SECTION 10: PREPOSITIONS AND LOCATIVES

### 10.1 Common Prepositions

| Nuer | English |
|------|---------|
| Rɛy | In, inside |
| Raar | Out, outside |
| Nhial | Above, sky, heaven |
| Piny | Below, under, earth, ground |
| Jɔk / Jɔɔk | Behind |
| Nhiam | In front of, before |
| Gekä | Beside, next to |
| Kä | From, and (connective) |
| Wëë | To, towards |
| Kɛ | With, for, by (instrumental) |
| Kɛɛ | With, by |
| Kɛnɛ | And, with (coordinating) |
| Kɛ ɣöö | Because |
| Luɔt / tuum | Opposite |
| Gua̱a̱th | Around, place |

> Examples:
> - *Tëë rɛy mäktäpä.* = "He is inside the office."
> - *Cuɛ jɛ la̱th rɛy kakä E-dɛn.* = "He put him in the Garden of Eden."
> - *Kä cuɛ kam pi̱i̱ni piɛny da̱a̱k.* = "He separated the waters below."
> - *Kä cuɛ wut tuɔ̱k raar rɛy kakä E-dɛn.* = "He drove the man out of Eden."

### 10.2 Directional Verbs

Several motion verbs carry directional meaning:
- *wä* = go (away from speaker)
- *ben / bën* = come (toward speaker)
- *riŋ* = run
- *jäl* = walk, go, travel
- *luny* = return, come back

## SECTION 11: CONJUNCTIONS AND DISCOURSE MARKERS

### 11.1 Coordinating Conjunctions

| Nuer | English |
|------|---------|
| Kä | And (narrative), but also "from" (as preposition) |
| Kɛnɛ | And (with), plus |
| Kiɛ | Or |
| Duŋdɛ ɣöö | But |
| Kɛ ɣöö | Because |

> From the Bible, **Kä** is the most common narrative connector (equivalent to the Hebrew "waw consecutive"):
> - *Kä cu Kuoth buay nɛn gɔaaɛ.* = "And God saw that the light was good."
> - *Kä cuɛ kam pi̱i̱ni piɛny da̱a̱k kɛnɛ pi̱ tin te nhial.* = "And he separated the waters below from the waters above."

### 11.2 Subordinating Conjunctions / Relative Markers

| Nuer | English |
|------|---------|
| mi | which, that, who (relative marker) |
| tin | which (plural relative, "those which") |
| mëë | when, after (temporal) |
| ɣöö | that (complementizer), so that, because |
| kɛ ɣöö | because, in order that |
| mɔ kɛ cätdɛ | according to its kind |
| ɛn ɣöö | because (more formal) |

> Examples:
> - *le̱y **mi** pɛl kɛ pɛl* = "creature **which** is crafty"
> - *jiɛn kakä **tin** gɔaa nëndiɛn* = "trees **that** were pleasing to the eye"
> - ***mëë** cak Kuoth Nhial ni Kuoth, nhial kɛnɛ piny* = "**when** the Lord God made the earth and heavens"
> - *Cu Kuoth ɛ lar **ɛn ɣöö** bi pi̱ tekɛ dääk* = "God made it so **that** the water would be separated"

| Nuer | English |

| Titi | These (plural) |
| Nɛmi / Nɛmɔ | That (singular) |
| Tɔ̱tɔ̱ | Those (plural) |
| gua̱th ɛ mɛ | Here |
| gua̱th ɛ mi̱i̱ | There |
| ɛn | This/that (in phrases), it, which |

> Examples:

## SECTION 13: NUMBERS

### 13.1 Cardinal Numbers

| Number | Nuer |
|--------|------|
| 0 | Baŋ |
| 1 | Kɛl / kɛl |
| 2 | Rɛw / da̱ŋ rɛw |
| 3 | Di̱ɔ̱k / da̱ŋ diɔ̱k |
| 4 | Ŋuaan / da̱ŋ ŋuaan |
| 5 | Dhieec / da̱ŋ dhieec |
| 6 | Bäkɛl / da̱ŋ bäkɛl |
| 7 | Bärɔw / da̱ŋ bärɔw |
| 8 | Bädäk / da̱ŋ bädäk |
| 9 | Bäŋuan / da̱ŋ bäŋuan |
| 10 | Thieer |

> **Number + noun order:** Number follows noun:
> - *Guɔ̱r **kɛl** wëë maath kɛ pi̱.* = "**One** elephant is going to drink water."
> - *Guëc **da̱ŋ rɛw** wäkɛ maath kɛ pi̱.* = "**Two** giraffes are going to drink water."
> - *mäthni **da̱ŋ ŋuaan*** = "**four** friends"

> **CRITICAL — kɛl means "ONE" (number), NOT the English adverb "just":**
> - **kɛl** = 1 / one / alone — it is a NUMERAL, not a discourse particle.
> - NEVER use **kɛl** to translate casual English "just" (e.g. "I will just sleep").
> - Example of correct use: *lony kɛl* = "one lion"; *ram kɛl* = "just one person / alone."
> - When English says "I will just sleep soon," DROP "just" entirely in Thok Nath: *Ɣän bä niɛɛn kɛ pɛ̈th.*

---

## SECTION 14: CONDITIONAL SENTENCES

Structure: **Mi + [condition clause], + [result clause]**

- *Mi ci ben, bi ben ŋiäc.* = "If you come, I will teach you."
- *Mi ci thiëc, bä ji luäk.* = "If you ask, I will help you."
- *Mi cä nɛn, bä la̱rɛ.* = "If I see him, I will tell him."
- *Mi ci nhial dɛ̈ɛ̈m, ciën bi ben.* = "If it rains, I will not come."
- *Mi wiaa jɛ wä cam, bi dhil li̱w.* = "When you eat it, you will certainly die." (Gen 2:17)

> **Rule:** The conditional word **Mi** ("if/when") introduces the condition. The result clause uses normal future or present markers.

## SECTION 16: COMPLETE SENTENCE EXAMPLES WITH ANALYSIS

### 16.1 Simple Declarative

**"Ni tukädɛ Kuoth cɛ Nhial kɛnɛ piny cak."**
= "In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth."
- *Ni tukädɛ* = "In the beginning" (locative phrase)
- *Kuoth* = "God" (subject)
- *cɛ* = past tense marker (3rd singular)
- *Nhial kɛnɛ piny* = "heavens and earth" (object, kɛnɛ = "and")
- *cak* = "created" (verb)

**"Ɛ ɣän ŋi̱i̱c."**
= "I am a teacher."
- *Ɛ* = copula (singular "is/am/are")
- *ɣän* = "I" (subject)
- *ŋi̱i̱c* = "teacher" (predicate noun)

**"Mɛmɛ ɛ maar."**
= "This is my mother."
- *Mɛmɛ* = "this" (demonstrative)
- *ɛ* = copula
- *maar* = "my mother" (possessive suffix on noun)

### 16.2 Past Narrative

**"Mandɔɔŋ cɛ dɔw jiaath nööŋ kä thuk."**
= "Grandmother brought fruit from the market."
- *Mandɔɔŋ* = "Grandmother" (subject)
- *cɛ* = past marker (3sg)
- *dɔw jiaath* = "fruit" (object)
- *nööŋ* = "brought" (verb)
- *kä thuk* = "from the market" (*kä* = from)

**"Cu Both kɛnɛ Nyayow ni̱n lɔ̱ŋä duëëlgɔ̱rä tin bi ben lip."**
= "Odongo and Apiyo waited for the school holidays to come."
- *Cu* = narrative past marker
- *Both kɛnɛ Nyayow* = "Odongo and Apiyo" (compound subject, kɛnɛ = and)
- *ni̱n lɔ̱ŋä* = "waited" (verb + object)
- *duëëlgɔ̱rä tin bi ben* = "school holidays which would come" (relative clause)
- *lip* = "to come, arrive"

### 16.3 Future

**"Ɣän bä wargak lääri̱ kuɛn i̱ruun."**
= "I will read newspaper tomorrow."
- *Ɣän* = "I"
- *bä* = future marker (1sg)
- *wargak lääri̱* = "newspaper" (object)
- *kuɛn* = "read" (verb)
- *i̱ruun* = "tomorrow" (time adverb)

### 16.4 Negation

**"Gaat /ci kɛn jɛ gör i̱ jiɛnkɛ."**
= "The children did not want to leave."
- *Gaat* = "children" (subject)
- */ci kɛn* = past negative marker (3pl)
- *jɛ gör* = "want it"
- *i̱ jiɛnkɛ* = "from there / to leave that place"

### 16.5 Relative Clause (with tin / mi)

**"Le̱y diaal tin tëk rɛy pi̱i̱ni"**
= "All living creatures that live in the water"
- *Le̱y diaal* = "all creatures"
- *tin* = "which/that" (plural relative marker)
- *tëk* = "live/exist" (verb)
- *rɛy pi̱i̱ni* = "in the water"

### 16.6 Imperative / Command

**"A ɣɔw tekɛ buay"** = "Let there be light" (Gen 1:3)
**"Ta̱yɛ kɛ gaat kä diëthɛ rɔ̱"** = "Be fruitful and increase in number"
**"Bër, canɛ ben kuën!"** = "Come, read with us!"
**"Jiɛc rɔ kä pat tetku nikä rɛɛw."** = "Stand up and clap your hands twice."

---

## SECTION 17: KEY GRAMMAR RULES — CONSOLIDATED

1. **No subject-verb agreement for number** — the verb root does NOT change for singular/plural. Only the tense/mood MARKER changes.

2. **Tense markers precede (or are part of) the verb phrase, not the verb itself.** The verb root stays the same across all persons; only the preceding marker changes.

3. **Word Order:** Flexible but generally: [Narrative Marker] + [Subject] + [Object] + [Verb] + [Time/Place].

4. **Questions** use the same word order as statements; only intonation (spoken) or "?" (written) marks interrogation.

5. **Copula "to be"** is **Ɛ** (singular subjects) / **Kɛ** (plural subjects) in the present. NOT expressed as a separate verb in past — **Ci̱** is used instead.

6. **Adjectives follow nouns.** The linker *mi* ("which is") introduces many adjectives: *wut mi di̱i̱t* = "the big man."

7. **Possessives are suffixes on nouns**, not separate words. The suffix vowel varies by person (-dä = my, -du = your, -dɛ = his/her, -da = our, -dun = your pl., -diɛn = their).

8. **Negation is a prefixed marker** that varies by person and tense. The marker is placed BEFORE the verb phrase.

9. **Narrative past marker "Cu/Cuɛ"** is placed before the subject in formal/Biblical prose. In ordinary past speech, the past marker is placed after the subject.

10. **Plural nouns** commonly add **-ni** or show vowel alternation. Adjectives used with plural nouns may also change form (ŋi̱i̱c → ŋi̱ääc).

11. **"And" is expressed differently:** *kɛnɛ* = "and" (between nouns/objects); *kä* = "and" (between clauses/sentences, narrative connector).

12. **Time expressions** typically come at the END of the sentence: *pan* = "yesterday," *i̱ruun* = "tomorrow," *walɛ / ɛn wa̱lɛ* = "today," *ni̱ ciaŋ* = "every day."

13. **Future tense covers future continuous.** Do NOT use the continuous verb form **wa̱a̱** in future sentences. The future marker **bä/bɛ/bi̱** already encodes "going to / will be doing." Use the simple verb root: *Ɣän bä wä lät i̱ruun.* = "I will be going to work tomorrow." (NOT *bä wa̱a̱ lät*)

14. **kɛl = ONE (number only).** Never use it to translate the English casual adverb "just." When English says "I will just sleep" or "I'll just go," drop "just" entirely in Thok Nath. It has no direct equivalent as a discourse particle.

15. **tëk functions as both verb and noun.** As a verb: *tëk* = "to live / to be alive." As a noun: *tëk* = "life." The context determines the reading. Example: *kä tëk* = "and live" (verb) OR "and life" (noun) depending on the sentence.

---

## SECTION 18: SAMPLE NEW SENTENCES (Applying the Rules)

The following sentences are constructed by applying the rules above:

| Nuer (constructed) | English | Rule applied |
|---|---|---|
| Ɛ ɣän geer. | I am a driver. | Present copula Ɛ + subject + noun |
| Jɛn ɛ ŋi̱i̱c. | He is a teacher. | Jɛn + ɛ (after subj) + noun |
| Kɛ kɔn ŋi̱ääc. | We are teachers. | Kɛ + plural subject + plural noun |
| /Ciɛɛ ɣän geer. | I am not a driver. | Present neg. copula |
| Ci̱ ɣän geer. | I was a driver. | Past copula Ci̱ |
| /Kän ɣän geer. | I was not a driver. | Past neg. copula |
| Ɣän cä wä rɛɛk pan. | I went to town yesterday. | Past marker cä + verb |
| Jɛn cɛ wä rɛɛk pan. | He went to town yesterday. | Past marker cɛ |
| Ɣän bä wä rɛɛk i̱ruun. | I will go to town tomorrow. | Future marker bä |
| Jɛn bɛ wä rɛɛk i̱ruun. | He will go to town tomorrow. | Future marker bɛ |
| La ɣän ɛ mi̱th ni̱ ciaŋ. | I eat every day. | Present La + subject + verb |
| Ɣän ɛ mi̱thä ni̱. | I am eating now. | Present continuous with -ä ending |
| Jɛn ɛ mi̱thɛ ni̱. | He/She is eating now. | Present continuous -ɛ ending |
| /Ci̱ ɣän wä rɛɛk. | I do not go to town. | Present negative /Ci̱ |
| /cɛ jɛn wä rɛɛk. | He does not go to town. | Present negative /cɛ |
| Ɣän ta̱a̱ kɛ bok. | I have a book. | "Have" ta̱a̱ for 1sg |
| Jɛn tëë kɛ bok. | He has a book. | "Have" tëë for 3sg |
| Ɣän /thiɛlɛ ɣä bok. | I do not have a book. | "Have not" thiɛlɛ |
| Mi ci ben dhɔrä, bä ji̱ ŋiäc. | If you come to my home, I will teach you. | Conditional Mi + bä |
| Mɛmɛ ɛ dämaar. | This is my brother. | Demonstrative + copula |
| Cuɛ bën kä mäktäp. | He came from the office. | Narrative past cuɛ + verb + preposition |

---


---

## SECTION 20: ADDITIONAL RULES DISCOVERED FROM DEEP READING

*(Sourced from: Nuer Bible — Psalms, Proverbs, Job, Genesis, Isaiah; African Storybook Project; Ethio Language Box Grammar)*

---

### 20.1 IMPERATIVES (Commands)

Thok Nath imperatives are formed by using the **bare verb root** directly, without a subject or tense marker.

| Form | Nuer | English | Source |
|------|------|---------|--------|
| Singular command | *Liŋ palä lö Kuoth* | "Listen to my prayer, O God" | Ps 55:1 |
| Singular command | *Liɛŋɛ jɛ* | "Listen/hear it" | Prov 8:6 |
| Singular command | *Puanyɛ Kuoth Nhial* | "Sing joyfully to the Lord" | Ps 33:1 |
| Singular command | *La̱rɛ Kuoth Nhial* | "Give thanks to the Lord" | Ps 136:1 |
| Singular command | *Päl gak, kä päl ŋɛ̈ɛ̈ny* | "Refrain from anger, turn from wrath" | Ps 37:8 |
| Singular command | *Wër* | "Go back / Return!" | Gen 31:3 |
| Plural command (to a group) | *Nyuthnikɔ nhökdu* | "Show us your unfailing love" | Ps 85:7 |
| Prohibition (negative imperative) | *Akɛ /ci jɛ ŋäth* | "Do not laugh at him" | ASB |
| Prohibition | *Akɛ /cu ɣä ɣɔ̱th mi la̱ŋä ji̱* | "Do not ignore my plea" | Ps 55:1 |

**Rules:**
- **Positive imperative**: bare verb root alone (no subject, no tense marker)
- **Negative imperative**: **Akɛ /ci** + verb OR **Akɛ /cu** + object + verb = "Do not [do V]"
- The suffix **-nikɔ** on an imperative verb = "for us / to us": *Nyuthnikɔ* = "Show [to] us"
- **lö** = vocative particle = "O [name]" — precedes who is being addressed

---

### 20.2 COMPARATIVE CONSTRUCTIONS — "ce̱tkɛ" (like / as)

**ce̱tkɛ** = "like, as, similar to" — the main comparison word in Thok Nath.

| Nuer | English | Source |
|------|---------|--------|
| *Ce̱tkɛ nikɛ jiath mi ca pith gekä yiëër* | "That person is like a tree planted by streams" | Ps 1:3 |
| *Ce̱tkɛ min la mac jiɛn a dɔp* | "As charcoal to embers [so is a quarrelsome person]" | Prov 26:21 |
| *Ce̱tkɛ min la ram mi näk buɔthɛ* | "As when a hungry person dreams" | Isa 29:8 |
| *Ce̱tkɛ gat mi /ka̱n dap* | "like a stillborn child" | Job 3:16 |

> **Rule:** Place **ce̱tkɛ** before the noun/clause being compared to. No equivalent of English "than" for comparisons — context carries the comparative meaning.

---

### 20.3 PURPOSE AND RESULT CLAUSES

**Two patterns for expressing purpose ("so that / in order to"):**

**Pattern A — kɛ ɣöö + future marker + verb:**
- *kɛ ɣöö bɛ jɛ luäk* = "so that he would help him"
- *kɛ ɣöö ba cätdiɛn yop a tëk* = "to keep their various kinds alive"
- *kɛ ɣöö bi kɛ yop a tëk kɛ ji̱ kɛɛl* = "to keep them alive with you" (Gen 6:19)

**Pattern B — kɛ ɣöö dëë + verb:**
- *kɛ ɣöö dëë gui̱l* = "to come and visit / so that he could visit" (ASB)
- *kɛ ɣöö dëë jiök* = "so that he could tell"
- *kɛ ɣöö dëë ji̱ ben poth* = "so that I may give you my blessing" (Gen 27:7)

> **Rule:** **kɛ ɣöö** (literally "because") introduces purpose/result clauses. When the purpose clause has a future/potential sense, the future marker (**bɛ/bä/bi̱**) appears after **kɛ ɣöö**.

---

### 20.4 SERIAL VERB CONSTRUCTIONS (Verb Chaining)

Thok Nath commonly chains verbs together — one verb of motion followed by another action:

| Nuer | English |
|------|---------|
| *wä nɛn* | go and see / go to see |
| *wä jiök* | go and tell |
| *wä gui̱l* | go and visit |
| *wä cam* | go and eat |
| *ben gui̱l* | come and visit |
| *ben näk* | come and kill |

**From Bible/ASB:**
- *Guäth ëë ci Thara ciek kua̱rä ni A-bɛ-ram dɔŋ* = "When my master's wife bore him a son in old age" — chaining noun + verb
- *Cu kɛn cuuc. Cu niɛɛn kɛ näk ɛ /kenkɛ mi̱eth* = "They were tired. They fell asleep before finishing dinner" (ASB)

> **Rule:** Motion verbs (**wä**, **ben**, **luny**) are regularly chained with a following verb to mean "go/come/return and [do V]." No conjunction is needed between the chained verbs.

---

### 20.5 VOCATIVE PARTICLE — "lö"

**lö** marks direct address — it is placed before the name/title of the person being spoken to:

- *Liŋ palä **lö** Kuoth* = "Listen to my prayer, **O God**"
- *lö ji̱ cuŋni* = "you righteous [ones]"
- *lö kuay jäŋädɛ ni A-bɛ-ram* = "you descendants of Abraham"
- *La̱rɛ **Kuoth Nhial** tɛ̈th lɔaac* (Ps 136:1) — sometimes without lö but same function

> **Rule:** **lö** = "O [addressee]" — vocative marker. Optional in informal speech but frequent in poetry, prayer, and commands.

---

### 20.6 INTENSIFIERS AND ADVERBS

| Nuer | English | Usage |
|------|---------|-------|
| **ɛlɔ̱ŋ** | very much, greatly | post-verbal: *nhɔakä **ɛlɔ̱ŋ*** = "like very much" |
| **amäni** | forever, eternally, always | *te thi̱n **amäni** cäŋ kɛl* = "will last forever" |
| **kɛɛliw** | altogether, all, completely | *cäkɛ jek tëk **kɛɛliw*** = "keep all their kinds alive" |
| **ni ciaŋ** | every day | *wä lät kɛ runwaŋ **ni ciaŋ*** = "go to work every morning" |
| **kärɔa** | alone, only, by himself/herself | *kärɔa* = "by himself alone" |
| **kɛ pɛ̈th** | soon, suddenly, quickly | *Kɛ pɛ̈th cu niɛɛn* = "Soon she fell asleep" |
| **ni̱ni** | truly, indeed, right now | *kɛ kɔr ni̱ni da̱ŋ bärɔw* = "Seven days from now" |
| **di̱t** / **ɛlɔ̱ŋ** | greatly, much (adverbial) | *nhɔk di̱t* = "love greatly" |

---

### 20.7 THE "BECOME" VERB — "cua̱"

**cua̱** expresses transformation, becoming, or a change of state:

| Nuer | English | Source |
|------|---------|--------|
| *cu raan cua̱ ram mi tëk* | "the man became a living being" | Gen 2:7 |
| *cua̱ jɛ do̱th* | "he was weaned / he grew" | Gen 21:8 |
| *cu buay cua̱ wal* | "light became distinct from dark" | Gen |
| *Cuɛ cua̱ cäŋ in [number]* | "It was the [Nth] day" | Genesis creation |

> **Rule:** **cua̱** = "became / turned into / resulted in." It is a **change-of-state verb**, used after the narrative marker **cu/cuɛ**. Pattern: **cu [subject] cua̱ [result noun/state]**.

---

### 20.8 REFLEXIVE THINKING AND INNER SPEECH

Thok Nath has specific patterns for expressing someone talking or thinking to themselves:

| Nuer | English | Source |
|------|---------|--------|
| *cuɛ rɔɔdɛ thiec i̱, "..."* | "She asked herself, '...'" | ASB |
| *cuɛ caarɛ jɛ i̱, "..."* | "He thought to himself, '...'" | Gen 41:32 |
| *cuɔ dhɔŋ ni ɣöö ɛ ruathda* | "I thought that it was one of our calves" | ASB |
| *cuɛ wee kɛ mi muɔ̱nɛ* | "as she breathed her last, she said" | Gen 35:18 |

> **Rule:**
> - **rɔɔdɛ thiec** = "ask oneself" (reflexive = "rɔ" + possessive suffix + thiec = ask)
> - **caarɛ jɛ i̱** = "thought to himself / said to himself" (Gen 17:17, 2Ki 20:19)
> - **lar kɛ lɔcdɛ** = "said in his heart" (lit. "spoke to his heart") — for God's or a person's inner speech (Gen 8:21)
> - **dhɔŋ ni ɣöö** = "I thought that..." (ASB: Lungfish story)
> - These are always followed by the quotation marker **i̱** and direct speech in quotes

---

### 20.9 PASSIVE AND PARTICIPIAL PATTERNS

**mëë ca + verb** = past passive participial ("that was [done]"):

| Nuer | English | Source |
|------|---------|--------|
| *jiath mi ca pith gekä yiëër* | "a tree **planted** by streams" | Ps 1:3 |
| *mëë ca raan kuɛn kɛ ji̱* | "what was found concerning you" | context |
| *duëël in cɛ raan puur thi̱n* | "the field that the person planted there" | |

> **Rule:** **mëë ca + verb** = "[that] was [verb]-ed" — completed/passive participial construction. This is how Thok Nath expresses passive meaning for completed events.

---

### 20.10 TIME EXPRESSIONS WITH "kɛ kɔr"

**kɛ kɔr** + time/event = "after [time/event]":

| Nuer | English | Source |
|------|---------|--------|
| *kɛ kɔr runi da̱ŋ rɛw* | "After two full years" | Gen 41:1 |
| *kɛ kɔr ni̱ni da̱ŋ bärɔw* | "Seven days from now" | Gen 7:4 |
| *kɛ kɔr thukä ni̱ni ti jiɛn ŋuaan* | "After forty days" | Gen 8:6 |
| *Kɛ kɔrɛ, Jɔk cuɛ li̱w* | "Then, Ajao died" | ASB |
| *Mëë ruɔ̱ndɛ* | "The next day / Early the next morning" | ASB |

> **Rule:** **kɛ kɔr + [time/event]** = "after [period/event]." The time noun/clause follows directly. **kɛ kɔrɛ** (with suffix) is used as a connector meaning "then/afterwards."

---

### 20.11 RELATIVE PRONOUNS — THREE FORMS

The current rules note "mi" and "tin." A third form also appears frequently:

| Form | Usage | Example |
|------|-------|---------|
| **mi** | singular relative (who/which/that) | *wut **mi** di̱i̱t* = "the big man" |
| **tin** | plural relative (those who/which) | *le̱y **tin** tëk* = "creatures that live" |
| **tëë** | third relative form (often before verbs) | *nɛy **tëë** te wi̱i̱ muɔ̱ɔ̱n* = "all people on earth" |
| **ti** | before negated verbs | *nɛy **ti** /ca guur* = "those who do not walk" |

> **Rule:** **tëë** and **ti** appear as relative markers before verb phrases, especially in longer relative clauses. **tëë** connects to affirmative verb phrases; **ti** (or **ti /ca**) appears before negated verbs in relative clauses.

---

### 20.12 BODY PARTS AS IDIOMS

Body parts frequently appear with possessive suffixes and carry figurative meanings:

| Nuer | Literal | Idiomatic / Figurative |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| **lɔc** + -suffix | heart | emotions, intentions, willingness |
| **lɔcdä** | my heart | "my desire, my will" |
| **lɔcdɛ** | his/her heart | "his feelings, his mind" |
| **puɔ̱nydɛ** | his spirit/soul | inner self |
| **thokdä** | my mouth | "what I say" |
| **wuɔ̱thnikiɛn** | their heads | "their leaders, their top" |
| **waŋdä** | my eyes | "my sight, my attention" |
| **riɛmdɛ** | his blood | "his life force, his essence" |
| **tëkdɛ** | his life | "his lifeblood" |

---

### 20.13 FUTURE NEGATIVE — STRUCTURE DETAIL

From ELB Grammar file — the future negative places the object BEFORE **bi̱**:

Pattern: **Subject + /negation + [object] + bi̱ + verb + time**

| Nuer | English |
|------|---------|
| *Ɣän /cän wargak lääri̱ **bi̱** kuɛn i̱ruun.* | I will not read newspaper tomorrow. |
| *Ji̱n /ci̱ wargak lääri̱ **bi̱** kuɛn i̱ruun.* | You will not read newspaper tomorrow. |
| *Jɛn /cɛ wargak lääri̱ **bi̱** kuɛn i̱ruun.* | He/She will not read newspaper tomorrow. |
| *Yiɛn /cia wargak lääri̱ **bi̱** kuɛn i̱ruun.* | You (pl.) will not read newspaper tomorrow. |

> **Key detail:** In future negatives, the bi̱ marker appears BETWEEN the object and the verb — unlike affirmative future where bä/bɛ comes after the subject.
> Also confirmed: **You (pl.) present negative = /cia** (alternative to /ci̱ yiɛn).

---

### 20.14 PAST CONTINUOUS NEGATIVE — STRUCTURE

Pattern: **Subject + /negative + kuën kɛ + object + ɛnëë**

| Nuer | English |
|------|---------|
| *Ɣän /ka̱n kuën kɛ wargak lääri̱ ɛnëë.* | I was not reading newspaper. |
| *Ji̱n /käni̱ kuën kɛ wargak lääri̱ ɛnëë.* | You were not reading newspaper. |
| *Jɛn /känɛ kuën kɛ wargak lääri̱ ɛnëë.* | He/She was not reading newspaper. |
| *Kɔn /kän nɛy kuën kɛ wargak lääri̱ ɛnëë.* | We were not reading newspaper. |

**With pronoun object (no kɛ needed):**

| *Ɣän /ka̱n jɛ la̱t ɛnëë.* | I was not making it. |
| *Kɔn /kän nɛyɛ la̱t ɛnëë.* | We were not making it. |
| *Ji̱n /käni̱ jɛ la̱t ɛnëë.* | You were not making it. |
| *Jɛn /känɛ jɛ la̱t ɛnëë.* | He/She was not making it. |

> **Key detail:** Past continuous negative uses the same negation markers as the regular past tense. With a **noun object**: NEG-marker + **verb-root** + **kɛ** + noun + **ɛnëë** (the particle "kɛ" links the verb to its noun object). With a **pronoun object**: NEG-marker + pronoun + verb-root + **ɛnëë** (no "kɛ" needed). The "kɛ" in `kuën kɛ wargak` is a linker particle, not part of a fixed phrase. Both patterns confirmed by ELB Grammar source.

---

### 20.15 KEY BIBLICAL VOCABULARY — FREQUENTLY RECURRING

| Nuer | English |
|------|---------|
| **tɛ̈th lɔaac** | Blessed / Praise |
| **cuŋ** / **cuŋni** | righteous / the upright |
| **ji̱ nyuɔɔni** | the wicked |
| **ji̱ dueeri** | sinners |
| **nhök** / **nhɔk** | love, compassion (God's love = **nhökdɛ min thil pek** = "unfailing love") |
| **gɔɔy** / **gɔɔydɛ** | holy, holiness |
| **cuŋdɛ** | his righteousness |
| **ruacdu** | your word / your law |
| **käändä** | my shelter / refuge |
| **gääŋdä** | my fortress / stronghold |
| **Kuoth Nhial ni Kuoth** | The Lord God (lit. "God the Lord as God") |
| **amäni cäŋ kɛl** | forever and ever (lit. "forever one day") |
| **kɛ ɣöö gɔaaɛ** | "for it is good" (Ps 136:1 refrain) |

---

### 20.16 PROVERB / WISDOM SENTENCE PATTERNS (from Proverbs/Job)

Proverbs and wisdom literature use distinctive two-part contrasting structures:

**Pattern: [Positive subject] + [positive result], kä [negative subject] + [negative result]**

| Nuer | English |
|------|---------|
| *Ram mi pɛl tiitdɛ luek, duundɛ ɣöö ram mi ruac dɔ̱ɔ̱rä bathɛ.* | "The wise in heart accept commands, but a chattering fool comes to ruin." |
| *Mi̱th gua̱n cuŋni ce̱tkɛ lɔcdɛ, kä ram mi lät jiäk näk buɔthɛ.* | "The righteous eat to their hearts' content, but the stomach of the wicked goes hungry." |
| *Kä ram mi wä mundɛ la̱t, bɛ tekɛ mi̱eth mi di̱i̱t, kä ram mi /ci lät, bɛ jek ni can.* | "Those who work their land will have abundant food, but those who chase fantasies will have their fill of poverty." |

**Pattern elements:**
- First clause: positive case (usually present tense with **la** or habitual marker)
- Connective: **kä** (and/but — contrastive)
- Second clause: negative/contrasting case
- **duundɛ ɣöö** = "but / however" (stronger contrast)

---


---

## SECTION 21: TRANSLITERATION OF FOREIGN NAMES INTO THOK NATH

*(Foreign country names, person names, and place names not originally in Thok Nath are written using the Nuer writing system. The rules below are derived directly from the Nuer Bible's established transliteration of Hebrew, Greek, and Aramaic names.)*

---

### 21.1 THE FOUNDATIONAL PRINCIPLE

Foreign names are **not borrowed unchanged**. They are adapted to fit Thok Nath phonology and writing. The Nuer Bible established this system for all Hebrew and Greek names, and the same rules extend to modern names (countries, cities, people).

> **Key source:** Every foreign proper noun in the Nuer Bible is transliterated — not left in its original form. We follow that same system for modern names.

---

### 21.2 SYLLABIFICATION — USE HYPHENS

Break the foreign name into syllables and separate them with hyphens, exactly as the Nuer Bible does:

| Original | Nuer Bible form |
|---|---|
| Abraham | **A-bɛ-ram** |
| Jerusalem | **Jɛ-ru-tha-lɛm** |
| Benjamin | **Ben-ya-min** |
| Assyria | **A-thi-ri-ya** |
| Lebanon | **Lɛ-ba-nɔn** |

> **Rule:** Every syllable of a foreign name gets its own hyphen-separated segment. This makes pronunciation clear and follows established Nuer Bible practice.

---

### 21.3 VOWEL MAPPING TABLE

| English vowel | Thok Nath equivalent | Bible example |
|---|---|---|
| a (open) | **a** | Abraham → A-bɛ-**ram** |
| e (short / open) | **ɛ** | Israel → I-thɛ-rɛl, Joseph → Jo-thɛp |
| i | **i** | Assyria → A-thi-**ri**-ya |
| o (rounded / long) | **ɔ** | Jordan → J**ɔ**r-dɛn, Solomon → Th**ɔ**-lo-mon |
| u | **u** or **ɔ** | Jerusalem → Jɛ-**ru**-tha-lɛm |
| ia / ea (ending) | **ya** | Assyria → A-thi-ri-**ya**, Benjamin → Ben-**ya**-min |
| H (word-initial) | **Ɣ** | Ham → **Ɣ**ɛ̈m |
| au / aw | **ɔ** | Australia → **O**th-rɛ-li-ya |

---

### 21.4 CONSONANT MAPPING TABLE

| English sound | Thok Nath | Confirmed by (Nuer Bible) |
|---|---|---|
| **s** | **th** | Solomon → **Th**ɔ-lo-mon; Moses → Mu**th**ɛ; Israel → I-**th**ɛ-rɛl; Joseph → Jo-**th**ɛp |
| **sh** | **c** | Shem → **C**ɛm; Ishmael → I-**c**a-mel |
| **H** (initial) | **Ɣ** | Ham → **Ɣ**ɛ̈m |
| **ph / f** | **p** | Ephrath → **Ɛp**-rath; Pharaoh → **P**ɛro |
| **c / ck / k** | **k** | Isaac → Ay-dhɛk |
| **j** [dʒ sound] | **j** | Jacob → **Je**-kɔb; John → **Jɔ̱ɔ̱n**; James → **Je-mɛth** (MAT 4:21) |
| **z** [z sound] | **dh** | Zebedee → **Dhɛ**-ba-dii; Zerubbabel → **Dhɛ**-ru-ba-bɛl |
| **ch** (as in "chin") | **c** | Following Shem → Cɛm pattern |
| **y** (consonant) | **y** | Benjamin → Ben-**ya**-min |
| **x** | **kth** | — |
| **q / qu** | **k** | — |

> **CRITICAL — s→th rule:** The letter **s** in a foreign name is written as **th** in Thok Nath. This is the single most important consonant rule. Confirmed across multiple Bible names (Solomon, Moses, Israel, Joseph, Assyria, Jerusalem).

> **CRITICAL — J vs Dh distinction:** The English **J** [dʒ] sound stays as **J** in Thok Nath — confirmed by NT Bible: John = **Jɔ̱ɔ̱n**, James = **Je-mɛth**, Jacob = **Je-kɔb**, Jordan = **Jɔr-dɛn**, Judea = **Ju-dia**. The **dh** digraph is reserved for the **Z** sound (Zebedee = **Dhɛ-ba-dii**, Zerubbabel = **Dhɛ-ru-ba-bɛl**). Never write J as Dh.

> **CRITICAL — Translate common words:** If part of a foreign proper noun is a common directional or descriptive word that has a Nuer equivalent, **translate** that word — do not transliterate it. Example: "South Sudan" → **Cuec** Thu-da̱n, because *Cuec* is the actual Nuer word for "south." Only the unique proper name part (Sudan) is transliterated.

---

### 21.5 MODERN COUNTRY NAMES — APPLIED EXAMPLES

| English | Syllables | Thok Nath | Rule applied |
|---|---|---|---|
| America | A-me-ri-ca | **A-mɛ-ri-ka** | e→ɛ, c→k |
| Korea | Ko-re-a | **Kɔ-rɛ-ya** | o→ɔ, e→ɛ, a→ya |
| Japan | Ja-pan | **Ja-paan** | J stays; stressed/long vowel → long **aa** |
| China | Chi-na | **Ci-na** | Ch→C |
| France | Fran-ce | **Pɛ-ranthi** | F→P, e→ɛ, ce→thi |
| Russia | Rus-si-a | **Rɔ-thi-ya** | u→ɔ, ss→th, ia→ya |
| Germany | Ger-ma-ny | **Jɛr-ma-ni** | e→ɛ, G soft→J, y→i |
| Australia | Aus-tra-li-a | **Oth-rɛ-li-ya** | Au→O, s→th, e→ɛ, ia→ya |
| India | In-di-a | **I̱n-di-ya** | ia→ya |
| Brazil | Bra-zil | **Bɛ-ra-dhil** | e→ɛ, z→dh |
| Sudan | Su-dan | **Thu-dan** | S→Th |
| Kenya | Ken-ya | **Kɛ-nya** | e→ɛ |
| Ethiopia | E-thi-o-pi-a | **I-thi-yo-pi-ya** | E→I, th stays, ia→ya |
| Uganda | U-gan-da | **U-gan-da** | stays close |
| Nigeria | Ni-ge-ri-a | **Ni-jɛ-ri-ya** | g→j, e→ɛ, ia→ya |
| Ghana | Gha-na | **Ɣa-na** | Gh→Ɣ |
| South Sudan | Cuec + Su-dan | **Cuec Thu-da̱n** | "South" = Nuer word **Cuec** (translate, don't transliterate); Sudan: S→Th, dan→da̱n (a̱ underbar vowel) |
| United States | U-ni-ted States | **U-ni-tɛd Thi-tɛth** | e→ɛ, S→Th, es→ɛth |
| United Kingdom | U-ni-ted King-dom | **U-ni-tɛd Kiŋ-dɔm** | e→ɛ, ng→ŋ, o→ɔ |

---

### 21.6 PERSON NAMES — ALL CONFIRMED FROM THE NUER BIBLE

**RULE: Always use the form the Nuer Bible already established. Never re-invent a name that the translators already settled.**

#### MALE NAMES

| English name | Thok Nath | Bible reference |
|---|---|---|
| John | **Jɔ̱ɔ̱n** | MAT 3:1, 3:13, 3:14, 4:21 ✓ |
| James | **Je-mɛth** | MAT 4:21: *Je-mɛth, kɛnɛ däman ni Jɔ̱ɔ̱n* ✓ |
| Peter | **Pi-tɛr** | e→ɛ |
| David | **Dee-bid** | Throughout OT ✓ |
| Moses | **Muthɛ** | Throughout Exodus ✓; S→Th |
| Samuel | **Thɛ-mu-ɛl** | S→Th, a→ɛ |
| Michael | **Mai-kɛl** | ae→ɛ |
| Joseph | **Jo-thɛp** | MAT 27:56 ✓; s→th |
| Jacob | **Je-kɔb** | GEN 29:10 ✓; J stays, o→ɔ |
| Paul | **Pɔl** | ACT 18:18 ✓ |
| Abraham | **A-bɛ-ram** | MAT 1:1 ✓ |
| Isaac | **Ay-dhɛk** | GEN 17:19 ✓; ck→k→dhɛk |
| Adam | **A-dam** | GEN 3:20 ✓ |

| English name | Thok Nath | Bible reference |
|---|---|---|
| Eve | **Iib** | GEN 3:20: *cu wut ciöt ciekdɛ cɔl i̱ Iib* ✓ |

| Miriam | **Mir-yam** | EXO 15:20: *Cu Mir-yam in la cääk din* ✓ |
| Hannah | **Ɣana** | 1SA 1:10: *cu Ɣana Kuoth Nhial pal* ✓; H→Ɣ |

### 21.7 "PERSON FROM [COUNTRY]" — THE raan rööl PATTERN

**Confirmed directly from the Nuer Bible:**
> Gen 23:4: *Ɛ ɣän **raan rööl** go̱lä* = "I am a foreigner / a person from another land"

**Pattern:** *raan rööl [country-name]* = "a person from [country]"

| English | Thok Nath |
|---|---|
| I am from America. | *Ɛ ɣän raan rööl A-mɛ-ri-ka.* |
| I am from Korea. | *Ɛ ɣän raan rööl Kɔ-rɛ-ya.* |
| She is from Japan. | *Ɛ jɛn raan rööl Ja-paan.* |
| He is from China. | *Ɛ jɛn raan rööl Ci-na.* |
| They are from Russia. | *Kɛ kɛn raan rööl Rɔ-thi-ya.* |
| We are from South Sudan. | *Kɛ kɔn raan rööl Cuec Thu-da̱n.* |
| Are you from Germany? | *Ɛ ji̱n raan rööl Jɛr-ma-ni?* |

---

### 21.8 CARDINAL DIRECTIONS — NUER WORDS (NOT TRANSLITERATED)

Directional words (north, south, east, west) are **never transliterated** — they are translated using the actual Nuer words confirmed in the Bible. When a place name contains a direction word, translate the direction and transliterate only the proper name.

All four cardinal directions have **single-word forms** confirmed in the Nuer Bible — just like *cuec* (south) is used alone in "Cuec Thu-da̱n," all four can be used as standalone words before a place name.

**PSA 89:12** — north and south (only two words, unambiguous):
> *"curi **cam ɣɔaa** kɛnɛ **cuec ɣɔaa** cak"* = *"You created the **north** and the **south**"*

**PSA 103:12** — east and west as single words (one of the most famous Bible verses):
> *"ce̱tnikɛ min nɔ̱a̱n **nhiam ɣɔaa** kɛ **jɔk ɣɔaa**"* = *"as far as the **east** is from the **west**"*

**LUK 13:29** — all four directions together:
> *"ben kui̱c känyä ca̱ŋ kɛnɛ kony ca̱ŋ, kɛ kui̱c **caam ɣɔaa** kɛnɛ **cuec ɣɔaa**"* = *"from east and west and **north** and **south**"*

| Direction | Thok Nath (single word) | Also used as | Meaning behind the word |
|---|---|---|---|
| **North** | **Caam** | — | LUK 13:29: *caam ɣɔaa* ✓; PSA 89:12 ✓✓; PSA 107:3 ✓✓ |
| **South** | **Cueec** | — | GEN 13:9: *cuëëc* ✓; PSA 89:12 ✓✓; PSA 107:3 ✓✓; LUK 13:29 ✓ |
| **East** | **Nhiam** | **käny ca̱ŋ** (compound phrase) | PSA 103:12 ✓✓; 2KI 10:33 ✓; DAN 8:9 ✓; DAN 11:44 ✓ — *nhiam* = "face/front" (facing the rising sun) |
| **West** | **Jɔk** | **kony ca̱ŋ** (compound phrase) | PSA 103:12 ✓✓ — *jɔk* = "back/behind" (behind the rising sun) |

> **CRITICAL — vowel length:** North = **Caam** (long aa), South = **Cueec** (long ue). The short forms *cam/cuec* appear in some Bible verses but the long vowel forms *caam/cueec* are the correct standalone direction words used in place names.

> **Note:** The compound forms **käny ca̱ŋ** (east) and **kony ca̱ŋ** (west) also appear frequently, especially in Genesis and Exodus. Both the single-word and compound forms are correct. For place name prefixes, the single words (nhiam, jɔk, cam, cuec) are cleaner and more consistent.

> **Note on tabernacle terms:** **kayŋuääk** (north side) and **targɛ̈w** (south side) appear in Exodus tabernacle construction only — not used for geographic names.

#### PLACE NAMES WITH DIRECTIONAL WORDS

**Pattern:** *[Direction word] + [Transliterated country/region name]*

| English | Thok Nath | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| South Sudan | **Cueec Thu-da̱n** | Cueec = south (long ue) |
| North Sudan | **Caam Thu-da̱n** | Caam = north (long aa) |
| South Africa | **Cueec A-pi-ri-ka** | Cueec = south |
| North Africa | **Caam A-pi-ri-ka** | Caam = north |
| East Africa | **Nhiam A-pi-ri-ka** | Nhiam = east (PSA 103:12) |
| West Africa | **Jɔk A-pi-ri-ka** | Jɔk = west (PSA 103:12) |
| South Korea | **Cueec Kɔ-rɛ-ya** | Cueec = south |
| North Korea | **Caam Kɔ-rɛ-ya** | Caam = north |
| East Asia | **Nhiam A-thia** | Nhiam = east; Asia: s→th |
| West Asia / Middle East | **Jɔk A-thia** | Jɔk = west |

---

#### NEW RULES CONFIRMED FROM NATIVE CORRECTION

**Rule A — Movement verbs go DIRECTLY into the place name (no "kä" needed):**

| Pattern | Example |
|---|---|
| Subject + **wä** + [place] | *Cu Jɔ̱ɔ̱n wä **Cueec Thu-da̱n*** = "John went to South Sudan" |
| Subject + **jiɛɛn** + [place] | *Cu Ɣana jiɛɛn **Jɔk A-pi-ri-ka*** = "Hannah came from West Africa" |

> "kä" before a place name is *not* needed with motion verbs (wä, jiɛɛn). The place follows the verb directly.

**Rule B — Pronoun comes BEFORE the future marker:**

| Wrong | Correct |
|---|---|
| *kä bɛ jɛn wä* | *kä **jɛn bɛ** wä* = "and she will go" |

> Order: Subject/Pronoun + **bɛ** (future) + verb — never bɛ before pronoun.

**Rule C — "arrived at / reached" = `wä`:**

| Example | Translation |
|---|---|
| *cukɛ wä Caam Thu-da̱n* | "they arrived in / went to North Sudan" |

> **wä** serves as both "go" (away from speaker) and "arrive/reach" a destination. Context determines which reading applies. Sometimes written as *we* (variant spelling), but *wä* is the standard form.

---

### 21.9 QUICK REFERENCE — THE MOST IMPORTANT RULES

> 1. **s → th** (the most critical rule: Solomon → Thɔ-lo-mon)
> 2. **e → ɛ** (open-mid front vowel: Israel → I-thɛ-rɛl)
> 3. **o → ɔ** (open-mid back vowel: Jordan → Jɔr-dɛn)
> 4. **ia / ea endings → ya** (Assyria → A-thi-ri-ya)
> 5. **f/ph → p** (Pharaoh → Pɛro, France → Pɛ-ranthi)
> 6. **Syllabify with hyphens** (A-bɛ-ram, not Abɛram)
> 7. **"I am from X" = Ɛ ɣän raan rööl [X].**

## SECTION 22: NEW RULES FROM FULL SOURCE DEEP-READ (Bible + ELB + ASB)

*(All rules in this section confirmed from at least one primary source. Sources cited inline.)*

---

### 22.1 COMPLETIVE / PERFECTIVE MARKER — thuk / thuɔ̱k

The verb **thuk** (or **thuɔ̱k**) = "finished / completed / done." It functions as a standalone verb OR as a perfective marker following another verb.

| Nuer | English | Source |
|---|---|---|
| *Cua nhial kɛnɛ piny cu **thuk** inɔ.* | "The heavens and earth were completed." | GEN 2:1 |
| *Cu Kuoth la̱tdɛ cu **thuk** kɛ bäkɛl.* | "By the seventh day God had **finished** his work." | GEN 2:2 |
| *Cä la̱tdä **thuk**.* | "I **finished** my work." | User passage |
| *Ci̱ la̱tdä **thuɔ̱k**.* | "I **finished** my work." (variant spelling) | User passage |
| *Kɛ pɛ̈th, cu ni̱n lɔ̱ŋä **thuɔ̱k**.* | "Soon, the holidays were over." | ASB |
| *kɛ ɣöö bi mi ca lar ɛ Kuäär a **thuɔ̱k*** | "to **fulfill** what the Lord said" | MAT 1:22 |

> **Pattern:** Subject + verb + **thuk/thuɔ̱k** = completed action. Also used as "fulfilled" in prophecy contexts. *thuk* and *thuɔ̱k* are spelling variants of the same word.

---

### 22.2 FIRST PERSON COMPLETED / PAST FORMS — Cä vs Ci̱

Two forms mark first-person past/completed actions:

| Form | Usage | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Cä** | First person completed action ("I did/have done") | *Cä la̱t ni la̱t kɛl* = "I did one miracle" (JHN 7:21) |
| **Ci̱** | First person past copula ("I was") | *Ci̱ ɣän kɔnɛ ŋi̱i̱c* = "I was a teacher" (ELB) |

> **Cä** = "I + completed verb." **Ci̱** = "I was" (copular past). Both appear in the user's passage: *"Cä la̱tdä thuk"* (I finished) and *"Ci̱ la̱tdä thuɔ̱k"* (variant).

---

### 22.3 TO BE — PAST TENSE FORMS (Positive and Negative)

**Past Positive (Ci̱ + Subject):** *(ELB Structures, confirmed)*

| Subject | Thok Nath | English |
|---|---|---|
| I | **Ci̱ ɣän** | I was |
| We | **Ci̱ nɛy** | We were |
| You (m/f) | **Ci̱ ji̱n** | You were |
| She/He | **Ci̱ jɛn** | She/He was |
| You (pl) | **Ci̱ yiɛn** | You were (pl) |
| They | **Ci̱ kɛn** | They were |

With complement: **Ci̱ + subject + kɔnɛ + [noun]**
- *Ci̱ ɣän kɔnɛ ŋi̱i̱c.* = "I was a teacher."
- *Ci̱ jɛn kɔnɛ geer.* = "He was a driver."

**Past Negative (/Kän + Subject):**

| Subject | Thok Nath | English |
|---|---|---|
| I | **/Kän ɣän** | I was not |
| We | **/Kän nɛy** | We were not |
| You (m/f) | **/Kän ji̱n** | You were not |
| She/He | **/Kän jɛn** | She/He was not |
| You (pl) | **/Kän yiɛn** | You were not (pl) |
| They | **/Kän kɛn** | They were not |

- */Kän ɣän kɔnɛ däktör.* = "I was not a doctor."
- */Kän jɛn kɔnɛ puur-ka̱a̱kni.* = "He was not a farmer."

**Present Negative (/Ciɛɛ + Subject / /Ci̱kɛ for plural):**

| Subject | Thok Nath | English |
|---|---|---|
| I | **/Ciɛɛ ɣän** | I am not |
| We | **/Ci̱kɛ kɔn** | We are not |
| You | **/Ciɛɛ ji̱n** | You are not |
| She/He | **/Ciɛɛ jɛn** | She/He is not |
| You (pl) | **/Ci̱kɛ yiɛn** | You (pl) are not |
| They | **/Ci̱kɛ kɛn** | They are not |

---

### 22.4 REFLEXIVE PRONOUNS — puɔ̱ny + possessive suffix

"Self / myself / himself" formed by **puɔ̱ny** + the possessive suffix for each person: *(ELB Structures)*

| English | Thok Nath |
|---|---|
| I myself | **Ɣän puɔ̱nydä** |
| We ourselves | **Kɔn puɔ̱nydan** |
| You yourself (m/f) | **Ji̱n puɔ̱nydu** |
| She herself | **Jɛn puɔ̱nydɛ** |
| He himself | **Jɛn puɔ̱nydɛ** |
| You (pl) yourselves | **Yiɛn puɔ̱nydun** |
| They themselves | **Kɛn puɔ̱nykiɛn** |

Examples:
- *Ɣän thɔalä ca̱y.* = "I myself make tea."
- *Jɛn puɔ̱nydɛ tho̱lɛ kɛ ca̱y.* = "He himself makes tea."
- *Ɣän cua̱ rɔ thiec kärɔa* = "I asked myself" (ASB)

### 22.5 PREPOSITIONS — SPATIAL (ELB Structures confirmed)

| Thok Nath | English | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **rɛy** | in / inside | *Jɛn tëë rɛy mäktäpä* = "He is inside the office" |
| **rɛy duɔ̱ɔ̱rä** | inside (lit.) | *Rɛy duɔ̱ɔ̱rä* = "Inside" |
| **rar duɔ̱ɔ̱rä** | outside | *Rar duɔ̱ɔ̱rä* = "Outside" |
| **nhiam** | in front of / before | *Nhiam luaak kuɔth* = "In front of the church" |
| **jɔk** | behind / after | *Jɔk duël kuɔth* = "Behind the church" |
| **tëë wị̈ị̈** | on top of / on | *Bok tëë wịị tharbëtä* = "The book is on the table" |
| **tëë piny** | under / below | *Bok tëë piny tharbëtä* = "The book is under the table" |
| **tëë nhiam** | above | *Tëë nhiam kä thäntigirëtni ti 30* = "Above 30 degrees" |
| **gekä** | beside / next to | *Jɛn guurɛ ni ɣä* = "He is next to me" |
| **gekä dɛ** | next to (him/her) | near / adjacent |
| **luɔt / tuum** | opposite | *Nhiam duël tɔwä yio̱o̱ni* = "Opposite the bank" |
| **kä** | from | *kä Nhiam A-pi-ri-ka* = "from East Africa" |
| **kɛ** | with / by means of | *lät kɛ ji̱c* = "made with hands" |

### 22.6 STORY OPENING CONVENTIONS (ASB + Bible)

Thok Nath narratives and stories open with specific time-framing phrases:

| Opening | English | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Cäŋ kɛl...** | "One day..." | JDG 9:8; LUK 8:22; LUK 20:1 ✓ |
| **Kɛ cäŋ kɛl...** | "One day..." (with particle) | ASB: *Kɛ cäŋ kɛl, cu buuk bën...* |
| **Tëëkɛ [subject] mi...** | "There was a [subject] who..." | ASB: *Tëëkɛ gua̱n kakä mi tekɛ thäk* = "A farmer had an old ox" |
| **Kɛ thiaŋ...** | "One evening..." | ASB: *Kɛ thiaŋ, cu thäk kacik jiök...* |
| **Rɛy thiaŋ...** | "In the evening..." | User passage |

---

### 22.7 TIME EXPRESSIONS — COMPREHENSIVE

| Thok Nath | English | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Cäŋ kɛl** | One day | Bible/ASB |
| **I̱ruun** | Tomorrow | ELB |
| **Kɛ pɛ̈th** | Soon / Suddenly | ASB: *Kɛ pɛ̈th, cu geer kaŋ koth* = "Suddenly, the driver blew the horn" |
| **Kɛ kɔr gua̱th mi tɔt** | After a while | ASB: *Kɛ kɔr gua̱th mi tɔt, cu Both kɛnɛ Nyayow niɛɛn kɛ näk* |
| **Rɛy thiaŋ** | In the evening | User passage |
| **Kɛ thiaŋ** | One evening | ASB |
| **cäŋ kɛɛliw** | All day | User passage + Bible |
| **Ni ciaŋ** | Every day / daily | Bible |
| **kɛ ni̱n lɔ̱ŋä thuɔ̱k** | When the days were over / at the end | ASB |
| **bakä ɣɔaa** | At dawn | GEN 19:15: *Ni bakä ɣɔaa* = "With the coming of dawn" |
| **kɛ kɔr kä mëë ci...** | After [event]... | ASB: *Kɛ kɔr kä mëë cɛ tɔ̱tɔ̱ la̱t* = "After she had done as told" |

### 22.8 EMOTION AND STATE VOCABULARY (ASB + Bible)

| Nuer | English | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **lɔcdɛ tɛɛth** / **tɛth lɔcdɛ** | heart was glad / happy | GEN 39:4; ASB; User passage |
| **lɔcdɛ jiääk** | heart was annoyed / upset | ASB: *Cu Manpalɛ̈k lɔcdɛ jiääk* = "Chicken was annoyed" |
| **cuuc** | tired / exhausted / wasted away | ASB: *Cu kɛn cuuc* = "They were tired"; GEN 47:13 |
| **/cɛ puɔ̱nydɛ jek ɛ gɔaa** | didn't feel well (lit. "self didn't go well") | ASB: *Lual /cɛ puɔ̱nydɛ jek ɛ gɔaa* |
| **lɔcdɛ jiɛɛn** | heart left/broke / was troubled | ASB: *cu lɔcdɛ jiɛɛn* = (heart left = became sad) |
| **Ɣää** | Yes / agreed | User passage |
| **ŋɛ̈ɛ̈ny** | threatened / warned | ASB: *Jio̱k Nyapëc cuɛ ŋɛ̈ɛ̈ny kɛ gua̱ndi̱t* = "Jackal threatened the old man" |
| **nhɔk / nhɔkɛ** | love / likes | ASB: *Määthdä ni Nyagɔaa nhɔkɛ kët* = "My friend likes to swim" |

### 22.9 NARRATIVE DISCOURSE MARKERS (Bible + ASB)

| Marker | Function | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **kä** | and / then / but (general connector) | most common discourse connector |
| **kä cuɛ** | and then he/she (narrative continuation) | *kä cuɛ cuuc* = "and then he rested" |
| **duundɛ ɣöö** | but / however (strong contrast) | *Kä duundɛ ɣöö cu Ab-ram ɛ loc i̱* = "But Abram said" (GEN 14:22) |
| **kä ɛ jɛn** | "and it was he/she who" (focus/emphasis) | *kä ɛ jɛn gua̱ndɔɔŋ...* = "and it was he who was the ancestor" (GEN 10:21) |
| **Täämɛ** | "Now / Meanwhile / At that time" (scene-setter) | *Täämɛ, cu Kuoth...* = "Now, God..." very frequent in Genesis |
| **Ɛ jɛn cuɛ** | "It was then that he/she..." (focusing) | *Ɛ jɛn cuɛ wut tuɔ̱k raar...* = "It was then that he placed the man..." |
| **Ɛ jɛ nɔ** | "Therefore / That is why" | *Ɛ jɛ nɔ...* = causal/result connector |
| **mëë cɛ / mëë ci** | "when / after" (temporal subordinator) | *mëë ci Lɔt cu jiɛɛn* = "After Lot had parted" |
| **Kɛ kɔrɛ** | "Then / After that" | ASB: *Kɛ kɔrɛ, cu Manpalɛ̈k röm kɛnɛ man Ci̱rci̱ɛr* = "Then Chicken met Millipede's mother" |

---

### 22.10 PLURAL NOUN FORMATION

Nouns form plurals through **vowel lengthening** or **-i / -ni suffix**:

| Singular | Plural | English |
|---|---|---|
| ŋi̱i̱c | **ŋi̱ääc** | teacher → teachers |
| gääth | **ga̱a̱th** | merchant → merchants |
| geer | **gëër** | driver → drivers |
| däktör | **däktöri** | doctor → doctors |
| wut | **wutni** | man → men |
| gat | **gaat** | child → children |
| raan | **nɛy** | person → people (suppletive) |
| ciëk / ciek | **jiɛɛni** | wife → wives |
| jiath | **jiaath** | tree → trees |

> **Pattern:** Most nouns add **-ni** or **-i** for plural. Some use vowel lengthening (geer→gëër). *raan/nɛy* is a suppletive pair (completely different words for singular/plural). The ELB confirms this system.

---

### 22.11 PASSAGE ANALYSIS — USER'S STORY TEXT

The following passage demonstrates many of the above rules working together:

> *"Cä la̱tdä thuk or Ci̱ la̱tdä thuɔ̱k. Cäŋ kɛl, cu wut mi ŋuɛ̈t wä lät. Cuɛ lät cäŋ kɛɛliw kä cuɛ cuuc. Rɛy thiaŋ, cuɛ ciekdɛ jiök i̱, "Cä la̱tdä thuk or Ci̱ la̱tdä thuɔ̱k. I̱ruun, kɔn bi̱ nɛy lɔ̱ŋ kɛɛl." Cu ciekdɛ lɔcdɛ tɛɛth kä cuɛ wee i̱, "Ɣää.""*

**Translation:**
> "I have finished my work. One day, a young man went to work. He worked all day and then rested. In the evening, his wife said to him, 'I have finished my work. Tomorrow, we will all gather together.' His wife's heart was glad and she said, 'Yes.'"

**Rule-by-rule breakdown:**

| Phrase | Rule |
|---|---|
| *Cä la̱tdä **thuk*** | Section 22.1 — thuk = completive "finished" |
| ***Cäŋ kɛl**, cu wut mi ŋuɛ̈t wä lät* | Section 22.6 — "One day" story opener + mi relative clause |
| *cuɛ lät **cäŋ kɛɛliw*** | Section 22.7 — "all day" time expression |
| *kä cuɛ **cuuc*** | Section 22.8 — cuuc = was tired/rested |
| ***Rɛy thiaŋ*** | Section 22.7 — "In the evening" |
| *cuɛ **ciekdɛ** jiök i̱* | Possessive suffix -dɛ (his wife); jiök = said to (Section 7) |
| ***I̱ruun**, kɔn bi̱ nɛy lɔ̱ŋ kɛɛl* | Time word first; future kɔn bi̱; lɔ̱ŋ kɛɛl = gather together |
| *Cu **ciekdɛ lɔcdɛ tɛɛth*** | Section 22.8 — heart was glad (emotion idiom) |
